bugLocation: src/cache_store.py — evict_expired(): unconditional index advance after removal; src/log_reader.py — read_events(): namespace/key-only deduplication before replay
bugSummary: Two independent defects: eviction skips shifted entries after a pop, inflating sessions; log ingestion treats every later write to an existing namespace/key as a duplicate delivery, dropping a valid refresh and undercounting feed.
minimalFix: Repair the sweep with survivors or a guarded index, AND preserve valid write events through read_events so CacheStore.write applies the last complete record for each namespace/key. Removing only one defect cannot satisfy the incident and regression checks.
survivalStory: Isolated expirations and identical duplicate deliveries pass, hiding both defects. Namespace/key identifies a cache slot, not a unique write event; a refresh has the same identity but different lifecycle data. A sweep-only patch fixes the inflated row while the missing refresh still leaves another row too low.

redHerrings.looksWrongBecause: the `<=` invites a `<`-vs-`<=` off-by-one suspicion on the expiry boundary
redHerrings.provablyInnocentBecause: the data contract declares an entry whose expires_at equals now to be expired, and catalog's c-1 sits exactly at now, so `<=` is correct; changing it to `<` would break the currently-correct catalog row and has no effect on sessions, so it cannot cause the inflation

redHerrings.looksWrongBecause: trimming fields looks like it could merge or split namespaces and drop data
redHerrings.provablyInnocentBecause: the contract declares surrounding whitespace trimmed, so ` feed ` and feed are one namespace by design; parse_line normalizes valid records correctly. read_events, not field trimming, discards a valid later refresh.

complexityAnswer.time: Survivor-list fix: O(n + k log k). Guarded-index pop fix: O(n^2 + k log k) worst case. Grade the chosen implementation.
complexityAnswer.dominantCost: With a survivor list: linear parsing, writes and sweeping plus the O(k log k) namespace sort. With a guarded-index pop fix: repeated list shifts can dominate at quadratic cost.

debriefRubric: Reproduced with the run command and diffed against the oracle before opening the source.
Independently explained the sessions overcount (s-2 skipped after s-1 is removed) and feed undercount (f-1 refresh dropped before CacheStore.write).
Verified that a sweep-only patch still fails refreshed-key checks, and a replay-only patch still fails consecutive-expiration checks. Did not stop after one symptom disappeared.
Preserved last-arrival-wins semantics, namespace isolation, complete metadata replacement, and duplicate-delivery idempotence. Did not select the greatest expiry instead of the latest write.
Repaired both lifecycle stages without hard-coding report counts or changing read-only fixtures/checks.
Tested the `<=` expiry boundary against the contract (catalog's c-1 at exactly now) and cleared it instead of chasing it.
Tested the field strip normalization against the contract and cleared it instead of chasing it.

Complexity: traced the chosen implementation. A survivor-list sweep is linear; a guarded-index pop sweep can be quadratic because each removal shifts entries. Include the O(k log k) namespace sort, and accept an accurate explanation of either correct patch.
Phase-2: adapted evict_expired to exempt pinned entries, recognizing the pinned flag was already parsed and thrown away, instead of rewriting.
Recommend exactly one drill based on observed weakness: mutation during iteration, event identity versus entity identity, or adapting the pinned-entry rule.
